fixes.explanation: That one's not in this passage. The people count heads and find that “…none of the residents of Jabesh-gilead were there.” That's the town they land on. Keep Jabesh-gilead in your pocket, baker, because it matters in the next verses.

Six hundred is a real number in this story, but it belongs to someone else. It's how many Benjamite men escaped to the rock of Rimmon (Judges 20:47). The women brought from Jabesh-gilead number four hundred. Verse 14 says there were not enough women for all of them.

That's lower than what the text says, friend. The men found “…four hundred young women who had not had relations with a man…” This is a heavy part of the story. Four hundred still isn't enough for everyone, as verse 14 says.

That's it. The elders say, “there is a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh…” They give the spot such careful directions that you could find it with your eyes closed. And the text calls it yearly, so it comes around every year.

The elders are the ones talking, but that's not what happens at Shiloh. What they point to is “…a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh…” So it's a feast, and it comes around every year. Nothing here says the elders hold a meeting there.

The fathers do come up, but not as the signal. The elders talk about what they'll say if the fathers or brothers “…come to us to complain…” and that's about after the Benjamites have already acted. What the Benjamites watch for is “…the daughters of Shiloh…” coming “…out to perform their dances…” Order matters in a plan like this, baker.

True. The Benjamites did as instructed, and the text says they “…went back to their own inheritance, rebuilt their cities, and settled in them.” After everything this tribe went through, I'm glad to see it back on its feet. The tribe has a place to live again, baker.
The text says they did. The Benjamites “…went back to their own inheritance, rebuilt their cities, and settled in them.” So they have their own land and cities again, baker.

Mizpah was where the oath was sworn, and the text doesn't send anybody back there. It says “…each of the Israelites returned from there to his own tribe and clan, each to his own inheritance.” They just go home, baker.
